blind_target.title: What you hear shapes how you think: Sound patterns change level of construal.
blind_target.evidence_quote: We tried to reproduce the mixed-design ANOVA result of the Sound Priming x Information Type or the interaction on the toaster preference. We acquired the data from the linked repository, however, no analysis scripts were available, therefore, we tried to repeat the analysis according to the manuscript. We managed to load SAS type data set into R, we followed the exclusion criteria (we managed to remove the 5 participants as described in the manuscript), and we believe that we identified the correct variables (however, the data documentation was very poor – only variable names). We performed the mixed ANOVA and we did not manage to obtain the corresponding results. We further found that we are unable to obtain individual condition means that would correspond to those reported in the manuscript. After those mishaps we terminated the analysis attempt.
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: We performed the mixed ANOVA and we did not manage to obtain the corresponding results. We further found that we are unable to obtain individual condition means that would correspond to those reported in the manuscript.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: We proceeded as previously, up to the point of fitting the mixed-design ANOVA model. Instead of using the aggregated measure of preference, we tested each of the 5 subscales separately. However, neither of the specifications resulted in a result that would reproduce the original study.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original author data produced comparable numerical output, but the focal interaction was F=1.157, p=.335 rather than F=3.47, p=.01. Analyses of each of five related dependent-variable subscales also did not recover the finding; poor variable documentation limits interpretation.

shipped.title_o: Relative Education and the Advantage of a College Degree
shipped.outcome_quote: Computational: "The coefficient on the key interaction of interest, Degree Proportion x BA Degree, is positive: β̂ = .088, t = 2.316, p = .019 ... This fails to replicate the original result."

blind_target.title: Relative Education and the Advantage of a College Degree.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The claim selected for reproduction from Horowitz (2018) is that while individuals with college experience use verbal skills more than those without a college background do, this advantage declines as the proportion of college-educated individuals increases.
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: This fails to replicate the original result. Some features of the regression are similar to the original: the sign and significance of all of the non-interacted degree proportion and education terms shown in the above table, as well as the interaction between degree proportion and Some College, No Degree match, and the 𝑅 2 value of . 326 is similar to the . 339 in the original paper. However, the coefficient on the interaction term between degree proportion and BA degree is of an opposite sign to what was expected by the replication criteria.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: The claim selected for the original study yielded a negative regression interaction term in the focal test, corresponding to an increased local degree proportion reducing the effect of holding a four-year degree on the use of verbal skills. The replication yielded a positive regression interaction term in the focal test, corresponding to an effect in a different pattern compared to the original study.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The re-created analysis of the same source data produces comparable numerical output but reverses the focal interaction. Independently reconstructed occupational matching, outcome factor construction and inclusion rules change the substantive finding, providing robustness challenges. No numbers directly copied from the original author data were needed for comparable output.

shipped.title_o: Solidaristic Unionism and Support for Redistribution in Contemporary Europe
shipped.outcome_quote: Computational: "the difference in predicted probabilities found in the reproduction test was 9.8 percentage points. Moreover, this difference was significant at the 0.1 percent level (p = 1.696e-07)... This replication of the claim was successful according to the SCORE criteria."

blind_target.evidence_quote: The claim selected for reproduction from Mosimann and Pontusson (2017) is that the effect of union membership on support for redistribution is most pronounced for high-wage workers who belong to unions that are responsive to the interests of low-wage workers.
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: While the replicated estimate of the difference in predicted probabilities is nearly identical to that of the original study (0.098 vs 0.097), levels exhibit small differences: 0.649 vs 0.608 for union members and 0.552 vs 0.511 for the nonunion members. Because these differences remain small (about 4 percentage points or 6–7 percent in relative terms), they can be attributed to the discrepancies between the reproduction and original regression samples.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: Section 24 of the preregistration document (https://osf.io/f8kjt/) suggests several exploratory analyses to test the sensitivity of the replication results to choices made to construct the reproduction sample.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The focal predicted-probability difference was recovered to a negligible difference (.098 versus .097), and the authors explicitly judged this a successful reproduction. Authors describe level differences as small despite an unresolved sample-construction discrepancy. Sensitivity analyses are only suggested, not reported as performed.

blind_target.title: A mother’s voice: Impacts of spousal communication training on child health investments.
blind_target.evidence_quote: In the present report prepared for the Institute for Replication (Brodeur et al., 2026), we investigate whether the authors’ analytical results are computationally reproducible and robust.

blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: Only the removal of trimming in Table 4 leads to one of the main results becoming marginally insignificant. shipped.title_o: The Morning After: Cabinet Instability and the Purging of Ministers after Failed Coup Attempts in Autocracies
shipped.outcome_quote: We find that the original findings were reproducible and robust.

blind_target.authors: Bokobza, L., Krishnarajan, S., Nyrup, J., Sakstrup, C. and Aaskoven, L.
blind_target.title: The morning after: cabinet instability and the purging of ministers after failed coup attempts in autocracies
blind_target.evidence_quote: We replicate the analysis provided in Bokobza et al. (2022).
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote:
The materials produced the exact same results as reported in the
paper and appendix. We could not detect any coding errors or other issues and the
reproduction was seamless.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote:
Using coup risk rather than coup attempts as main independent variable (IV)
does not significantly affect the results when using country-fixed effects. However, when
the models are estimated using leader-fixed effects, the results are no longer significant.
This invites future research to explore the differences between coup attempts and coup
risk as drivers of purges.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original numbers were exactly recovered. Although the abstract and conclusion summarize the findings as robust, the alternative coup-risk specification removes significance under leader fixed effects; additional coup-proofing controls also remove significance in the all-controls country model. These are substantive qualifications under the axis rule requiring at least one reasonable alternative, hence robustness challenges.
